section_summary: This section concerns Japanese patents, trademarks, trade names and copyrights from the end of the war through 1949. American firms and trade groups report infringement and seek restored rights, while State, Army and occupation officials develop policies for registration, renewal and protection. The section also contains a Japanese patent specification, a report on Japanese trademarks in Morocco, proposed treaty language and duplicate copies of several records.

subfiles.title: Japanese patent in Chile
subfiles.about: The FBI forwards information on Katsuyuki Hikami’s Japanese patent found in a former Japanese firm’s Santiago records.
subfiles.summary: Forwards a patent memorandum.

subfiles.title: A Method of Preventing a Natural Combustion and Overheating of Sulphide Ores and Other Mineral Products
subfiles.about: The specification proposes applying soap to sulphide ores to prevent spontaneous heating and combustion.
subfiles.summary: Describes a protective coating formed when soap reacts with metal sulphates on ore particles; claims a method for suppressing oxidation.

subfiles.title: Japanese imitation of American products and marks
subfiles.about: Jacobi urges effective Japanese trademark and patent protections in postwar arrangements.
subfiles.summary: Cites counterfeit American brands and falsely labelled bourbon and rye whiskey.

subfiles.title: Reply to Lester E. Jacobi
subfiles.about: The State Department acknowledges Jacobi’s proposals concerning Japanese imitation and infringement.
subfiles.summary: Says the proposals have been recorded and will receive consideration.

subfiles.title: Charge slip for Henry Ruhl correspondence
subfiles.about: A file charge slip tracks the Henry Ruhl enclosure.
subfiles.summary: Records file 894.543 and an April 1946 charge.

subfiles.title: Note on delayed reply to Henry Ruhl
subfiles.about: A staff member explains revisions and delay in answering Henry Ruhl.
subfiles.summary: Says Miss Hadley passed on Ruhl’s letter and a draft reply.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning the ABC trademark
subfiles.about: The Department explains that U.S. military authorities cannot register trademarks in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Says private trade has not resumed and future registration opportunities will be announced publicly.

subfiles.title: Inquiry concerning the ABC trademark
subfiles.about: Ruhl asks how his client can protect its ABC textile trademark in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Reports a competing Japanese registration and asks about filing through U.S. military authorities in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Japanese assets and trademarks in Tangier
subfiles.about: The telegram lists Japanese-owned trademarks and other known Japanese assets in Tangier and Spanish Morocco.
subfiles.summary: Identifies registrations by two Japanese firms, says their value is unknown, and reports no other known assets or captured supplies.

subfiles.title: Cover letter to Raymond Vernon on peace treaty recommendations
subfiles.about: Ladas sends association recommendations on industrial property clauses for the Japanese peace treaty.
subfiles.summary: Requests information on treaty drafting.

subfiles.title: Reply to Ladas on industrial property
subfiles.about: Vernon acknowledges association recommendations for the Japanese peace treaty.
subfiles.summary: Says they are under study and U.S. treaty drafting is underway.

subfiles.title: Further reply to Ladas
subfiles.about: The Department assures Ladas that trademark proposals will receive serious consideration.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges proposed trade mark provisions for the peace treaty.

subfiles.title: Trade mark and unfair competition provisions for treaty with Japan
subfiles.about: The trade mark association proposes treaty provisions against confusing marks, unfair competition and false origin claims.
subfiles.summary: Describes Japanese trademark decisions based narrowly on ideographic transliteration and alleged deceptive origin markings. Proposes cancellation of confusing marks, safeguards against unfair competition and clear country-of-origin labels.

subfiles.title: General Inter-American Convention for Trade-Mark and Commercial Protection, selected chapters
subfiles.about: The enclosure supplies model provisions on commercial names, unfair competition, false geographical origin and remedies.
subfiles.summary: Articles 14–31 define protected commercial names, prohibit deceptive names and markings, and provide opposition, injunction, damages and seizure remedies. The excerpt supports the association’s proposed Japanese treaty terms.

subfiles.title: Japanese trademark Permutit
subfiles.about: Sebald reports the occupation authorities’ findings on alleged infringement of the Permutit trademark.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese government says the marks were cancelled in 1942 and unused by a Japanese firm; Permutit Co., Ltd. planned a name change. A general restoration policy remained pending.

subfiles.title: Japanese patent and trademark rights
subfiles.about: Mock urges treaty protection against prewar discrimination by the Japanese Patent Office.
subfiles.summary: Alleges systematic preference for Japanese applicants in patent and trademark disputes.

subfiles.title: Reply to Hugo Mock
subfiles.about: Vernon responds to Mock’s request for treaty protection of foreign industrial property rights.
subfiles.summary: Says the Department plans treaty provisions and occupation authorities may act sooner.

subfiles.title: Elizabeth Arden trademark infringement
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch transmits a directive concerning infringement by Arden Beauty Salon in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Reports an order requiring Japan to stop infringement and report its action.

subfiles.title: SCAP directive on Elizabeth Arden trademarks
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: SCAP directs Japan to prevent Arden Beauty Salon’s infringement of Elizabeth Arden’s marks and name.
subfiles.summary: Requires a compliance report within thirty days.

subfiles.title: Inquiry on filing trademark applications
subfiles.about: Drews asks whether U.S. citizens may file trademarks in Japan and requests attorney referrals.
subfiles.summary: Seeks current filing rules and reputable Japanese patent attorneys.

subfiles.title: Reply to Gustav Drews
subfiles.about: Vernon explains the current restriction and expected opening of Japanese trademark filing.
subfiles.summary: Says U.S. citizens cannot yet file, but applications may be allowed before year’s end.

subfiles.title: Transfer sheet for Gustav Drews correspondence
subfiles.about: A record-control form notes transfer of Gustav Drews correspondence.
subfiles.summary: Records a file transfer and analyst’s initials.

subfiles.title: Inquiry on Japanese patents and trademarks
subfiles.about: American Chemical Paint Company requests timing and rules for filing in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Asks when patent and trademark applications can be filed.

subfiles.title: Reply to R. W. Gannon
subfiles.about: Vernon outlines proposed restoration and new filing policies for foreign patent and trademark owners.
subfiles.summary: Patent policy awaits other governments’ concurrence; trademark policy is less advanced. Filing procedures will be announced publicly.

subfiles.title: Complaint about similar Japanese corn products trade names
subfiles.about: Corn Products Refining Company alleges a new Japanese firm’s name is confusingly similar to its subsidiary’s.
subfiles.summary: Requests State Department assistance against alleged unfair competition.

subfiles.title: Initial reply to Warren S. Adams
subfiles.about: Vernon acknowledges the trade name complaint and reports its referral for investigation.
subfiles.summary: Says the Army has been asked to investigate in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Proposed policy on treatment of Japanese trademarks
subfiles.about: Saltzman submits a State–Army trademark policy paper for Army approval.
subfiles.summary: Requests an early response before seeking Far Eastern Commission approval.

subfiles.title: Routing memorandum for Japanese trademark policy
subfiles.about: Auchincloss routes a cleared policy letter, paper and explanatory memorandum.
subfiles.summary: Requests Saltzman’s signature on the Army letter.

subfiles.title: Summary of proposed Japanese trademark policy
subfiles.about: Dixon summarizes four issues addressed by the proposed U.S. position on Japanese trademarks.
subfiles.summary: Covers deceptive marks and origin claims, marks of reconstituted firms, restoration of Allied rights, and Japanese rights abroad.

subfiles.title: Summary of proposed Japanese trademark policy, duplicate copy
subfiles.about: A second copy repeats Dixon’s summary of the proposed U.S. trademark policy.
subfiles.summary: Reviews deceptive practices, reconstituted firms, Allied rights in Japan and Japanese rights abroad.

subfiles.title: Army concurrence in Japanese trademark policy
subfiles.about: The Army accepts the revised joint policy and asks to be informed of other agency concurrence.
subfiles.summary: Confirms the revisions do not alter the draft’s substance.

subfiles.title: Army report on Corn Products trade name
subfiles.about: The Army reports that SCAP has ordered action concerning the disputed Japanese trade name.
subfiles.summary: Encloses SCAP’s notice that Japan must prevent continued use of a similar name.

subfiles.title: SCAP investigation of corn products trade names
subfiles.from: R. M. Levy, for the Supreme Commander
subfiles.to: Adjutant General, Department of the Army
subfiles.about: SCAP reports a directive to prevent use of a name similar to the American subsidiary’s.
subfiles.summary: Promises details when the Japanese government reports its action.

subfiles.title: Initial reply to Warren S. Adams, duplicate copy
subfiles.about: A poor copy repeats the Department’s acknowledgment and referral of the trade name complaint.
subfiles.summary: Says the Army was asked to investigate.

subfiles.title: Corn Products trade name complaint, copy
subfiles.about: A copy repeats Corn Products Refining Company’s complaint about a confusingly similar Japanese name.
subfiles.summary: Requests help against alleged unfair competition.

subfiles.title: Request for SCAP investigation of corn products trade names
subfiles.to: Civil Affairs Division, Department of the Army
subfiles.about: State requests investigation of alleged unfair competition between two Japanese corn products firms.
subfiles.summary: Asks Army to seek SCAP action if Japanese law is violated.

subfiles.title: Final reply to Warren S. Adams
subfiles.about: Vernon reports action taken on the Corn Products trade name complaint.
subfiles.summary: Says Japan has been directed to prevent continued use of a similar name.

subfiles.title: Inquiry on wartime cancellation of American trademarks
subfiles.about: Brady asks whether American trademarks were cancelled during the war and how owners can protect them.
subfiles.summary: Cites a member’s registrations due for renewal in later years.

subfiles.title: Reply on foreign trademark restoration
subfiles.about: Vernon explains wartime cancellations, lapses and planned restoration of foreign-owned trademarks.
subfiles.summary: Says just over fifty foreign-owned marks were cancelled; more lapsed for unpaid fees. Restoration on application is planned.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment from Corn Products Refining Company
subfiles.about: Adams thanks Vernon for handling the Japanese trade name dispute.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges receipt of the December 22 reply.

subfiles.title: Request for Office of Alien Property concurrence
subfiles.about: Thorp requests review of the agreed State–Army Japanese trademark policy.
subfiles.summary: Highlights provisions on Japanese rights abroad and seeks an early reply.

subfiles.title: Submission of recommendations on Japanese intellectual property
subfiles.about: The Far East-America Council submits recommendations on Japanese trademarks, patents and copyrights.
subfiles.summary: Seeks consideration during resumption of private trade and foreign investment.

subfiles.title: Recommendations on Japan trade-marks, patents and copyrights
subfiles.from: Far East-America Council of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.about: The council proposes postwar legal changes to protect American trademarks, patents and copyrights in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Calls for judging trademark similarity by sound and appearance as well as Japanese transliteration, and for curbing false origin claims and unfair competition. Proposes cancellation of infringing wartime registrations, renewal and priority periods, restored and extended patents, and stronger copyright protection. It also urges replacing the 1905 translation arrangement.

subfiles.title: Inquiry on renewal of prewar trademarks
subfiles.about: Brady asks if Americans may renew prewar Japanese trademark registrations that survived the war.
subfiles.summary: Requests the present renewal procedure.

subfiles.title: Interim reply to Joseph B. Brady
subfiles.about: Dixon says the trademark renewal question has been referred to the Military Government in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Promises a further reply.

subfiles.title: Further reply on trademark renewal
subfiles.about: Dixon reports that renewal is currently unavailable but a permitting policy is expected soon.
subfiles.summary: Conveys the Army’s advice on pending renewal policy.

subfiles.title: Reply to Arthur B. Foye
subfiles.about: Dixon acknowledges the council’s recommendations and describes progress on patent, trademark and copyright policy.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a patent policy press release and says trademark and copyright proposals remain under consideration.

subfiles.title: Office of Alien Property response on Japanese trademark policy
subfiles.about: The Office of Alien Property agrees with the joint policy subject to limits on its powers and licensing practice.
subfiles.summary: Bazelon says existing authority does not itself prohibit trademark use or guarantee royalty-free licenses. Licenses would be considered case by case, with flexibility for vested Japanese interests in U.S. corporations. His office concurs with the policy.

subfiles.title: Transmittal memorandum on approved trademark policy
subfiles.about: Dixon routes a letter advising Army of Office of Alien Property concurrence.
subfiles.summary: Requests transmission of policy conclusions to SCAP.

subfiles.title: Recommendation to sign Army policy letter
subfiles.about: Bishop recommends signing the Army letter after Office of Alien Property concurrence.
subfiles.summary: Refers to Dixon’s attached explanation and prior Department approval.

subfiles.title: Elizabeth Arden infringement despatch, duplicate copy
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: A second copy transmits the SCAP order concerning Arden Beauty Salon.
subfiles.summary: Requires Japan to stop infringement and report compliance.

subfiles.title: SCAP directive on Elizabeth Arden, duplicate copy
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: A second copy orders action against infringement of Elizabeth Arden’s trademark and trade name.
subfiles.summary: Directs a compliance report within thirty days.

subfiles.title: Permutit despatch, duplicate copy
subfiles.about: A second copy reports findings on the Permutit trademark and company name.
subfiles.summary: Repeats that the marks were cancelled in 1942, a Japanese company planned a name change, and a restoration policy was pending.

subfiles.title: Note on Elizabeth Arden infringement
subfiles.about: A handwritten note summarizes SCAP’s order concerning Elizabeth Arden and Arden Beauty Salon.
subfiles.summary: Notes corrective measures against further infringement in Tokyo.
